observation.visible_scene: A large arched wall built from interlocking multicolored plastic blocks (green, yellow, red, magenta, blue, purple columns) stands on a light wooden floor against a plain wall with a baseboard. A neat row of upright white domino-like pieces spans the top of the arch, and a separate curved line of white dominoes lies on the floor to the right. A small pile of loose colored and white blocks sits on the floor at the far left.
visible_changes: The row of white pieces on top of the arch topples progressively from the left end rightward: the leftmost white pieces are already tilted in the earliest frames and the fallen/leaning zone advances along the top as time increases, while the right end of the white row stays upright through the last frame.

The left vertical edge of the colored wall leans outward and collapses, with its blocks tumbling onto the floor and adding to the left-hand scatter pile; this collapse grows from roughly the middle of the excerpt to the end.
The right portion of the colored wall and the curved white domino line on the right remain standing and unchanged throughout.
The background (wall, baseboard, floor planks) does not shift, indicating the motion is object motion rather than camera motion.
The left floor pile of loose blocks enlarges as more pieces fall into it.
outside_clip_unknowns: What initiated the toppling (no hand, tool, or impact source is visible within the segment).
Whether the collapse continues past the right side after the clip ends, or whether the remaining upright sections eventually fall.
The state of the structure before t=0 (the leftmost white piece already appears disturbed at the first sampled frame).
uncertain_details: The exact frame at which the left colored column first begins to move is hard to pinpoint because early motion is subtle.
Individual small blocks bouncing or sliding on the floor are motion-blurred and their final resting positions are not fully resolved.
